newsitem.title: UK: BA dismisses talk of JAL alignment.
newsitem.headline: BA dismisses talk of JAL alignment.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Thursday there was definitely no foundation in a reported allegation by Virgin chairman Richard Branson that BA was planning to extend its alliance plans with AMR Corp's American Airlines to include Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL).
BA spokesman David Wilson said in London that Branson's comments, reported from Hong Kong by the Financial Times newspaper, were "news to us".
"In the case of JAL, there is very definitely no such alignment on the horizon. Alliances are neither in place nor even contemplated with JAL," he added.

Adding to a denial made in the same Financial Times article by BA chief executive Bob Ayling, who is also touring the Far East at present, Wilson said BA did not know of any agreement with JAL, which Branson was quoted as saying he had been told of by unnamed "Japanese ministry officials".
"We haven't heard about such (an agreement) and we haven't received it. We would like to see it," he added.
Branson, whose Virgin Atlantic airline is BA's only British-owned longhaul rival, has criticised the BA/American alliance plan relentlessly since it was announced in June.
JAL has an established link with American.
Wilson said it was apparent that in the aftermath of any American alliance, BA would need to address a weakness in its global network in the north Pacific region in some way.
"We have no plans to progress this until the American Airlines alliance is approved," he added.
American and BA have said they hope to get regulatory clearance in time to start the main alliance elements, including combining Atlantic passenger services, next April.
Japan's other large longhaul carrier, All Nippon Airways, has a frequent flyer link to British Airways as well as a link with Delta Air Lines Inc of the U.S..
In the complex web of hundreds of regional and local alliances between different airlines, Virgin has no clear Japanese linkage as yet, but does have a partnership with Delta on the Atlantic.
